issues.legal_issue: A decree obtained by deliberately withholding a material document to gain an advantage is obtained by fraud and is a nullity.
material_facts: The claimant had executed a registered deed relinquishing his rights in the disputed property to another person.
He later sought partition of the property without disclosing the deed or mentioning it at trial, while claiming an interest in the property.
The opposing parties discovered the deed when the claimant sought a final decree and relied on it to challenge the preliminary decree for fraud.
The trial court dismissed the application for a final decree, but the High Court reversed that decision.
issues.conclusion: The claimant obtained the preliminary decree by fraud because he concealed a vital document to gain an advantage. The decree was a nullity; the appeal was allowed, the High Court judgment was set aside, and the trial court’s dismissal was restored.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment or decree obtained by fraud on the court is a nullity and may be challenged even in collateral proceedings. A litigant must come to court with clean hands and produce documents executed by the litigant that are relevant to the litigation. Deliberately withholding a vital document to gain an advantage is fraud on the court and the opposing party; the opposing party’s ability to discover the document does not excuse the concealment. The court applied these settled principles and the clean-hands principle; the judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier judicial decision as authority for this ruling.

rule.if: fraud_challenge_to_decree and claimant_withheld_executed_document and document_material_to_claim and concealment_sought_advantage

predicates.fraud_challenge_to_decree: The proceeding challenges a decree on the ground that it was obtained by fraud.
predicates.claimant_withheld_executed_document: The claimant did not disclose or produce a document that the claimant had executed.
predicates.document_material_to_claim: The withheld document was relevant to whether the claimant had a right supporting the claim.
predicates.concealment_sought_advantage: The claimant concealed the document in order to gain an advantage in the litigation.

issues.definition: When a decree is challenged for fraud and the claimant conceals an executed document material to the claim in order to gain an advantage, the decree is treated as a nullity.
